flat_four: Builds a deterministic area-weighted proposal of four distinct physical filament colors from the selected material family.
Creates no mixed-color recipes and writes only physical F1-F4 color states to a Flat Four 3MF.
Projects legacy mixed manual-paint state at the Flat export boundary without rewriting the caller's canonical color state.

Persists the six deleted automatic F1-F4 pair tombstones used by Snapmaker Orca 2.3.5, preventing its application-wide automatic-gradient preference from recreating six visible 50/50 mixed rows while keeping every printable state in F1-F4.

Applies a Flat-Four-only conservative chromatic-shadow recovery pass: source faces assigned to a neutral physical slot may move to an enabled chromatic F1-F4 slot only when RGB span, Lab chroma, and normalized-RGB margin all retain clear material-colour evidence; near-neutral black remains excluded.

Manual Fill compares Flat Four's visible physical-state projection for connectivity, so connected legacy mixed IDs that appear as the same black region can be repainted together while canonical overrides, Full Spectrum boundaries, part masks, and Undo/Redo remain intact.

For a newly opened model whose automatic palette remains untouched, switching Full Spectrum / Flat Four recomputes the four-filament proposal for the target mode, so the result no longer depends on the mode active at file-open time; any manual filament, recipe, state, output, or palette-inheritance edit disables that refresh and is preserved.

The published Flat Four Test 3 prerelease does not remove white globally: meaningful small white targets such as eye whites beside dark linework remain unabsorbed, while only small high-confidence white/gray lighting islands on smooth chromatic surfaces are folded into the chromatic physical slot used around their boundary.

Retained white covering at least 0.01% of total printable area reserves a suitable near-white physical filament. White below 0.01% remains unabsorbed but does not by itself force a white spool and may map to the nearest selected F1-F4 colour.
Four physical F1-F4 slots and 3MF state metadata remain present even when an output effectively uses three paint IDs; manual paint remains authoritative and Full Spectrum behavior is unchanged.
illustration_filter: Offers experimental Cel Colour and Shaded Monochrome modes with fixed-front, geometry-aware stepped shading.
Bakes ordinary printable RGB targets without changing geometry, parts, or canonical manual paint.
Does not generate authored line art, PBR material response, or texture detail absent from the source colors; results depend on mesh normals and source data.
large_static_glb: Keeps the normal 512 MiB, 3,000,000-vertex, and 3,000,000-triangle limits.
A separate beta path admits only static TRIANGLES scenes from 3,000,001 through 5,000,000 triangles after explicit confirmation and with face-count adjustment enabled.
The reduced working model is limited to 450,000 faces; unsupported, ambiguous, changed, or over-limit input fails closed, and reduction can remove fine geometry or baked texture detail.

manual_editing: All drawing tools, colour selection, brush diameter, and fill actions are collected in the Brush panel.

Manual-paint batches use local effective-state lookup and compatible layered Airbrush batches traverse the adaptive tree once, with a proven sequential fallback.
The optimized path preserves encoded output, changed roots, overrides, adaptive trees, and Undo/Redo semantics.

output: Explicit Solidify supports a single GLB without Tripo part markers when its apparent openings prove to be exact 1:1 reversed boundary pairs at coincident UV or texture seams.
The single GLB seam weld runs before cleanup and QEM so face-count reduction cannot destroy the exact seam proof.
The seam path preserves every ordered triangle and part ID and does not add caps; ambiguous seams, non-manifold results, or true holes fail closed without replacing the current geometry.

Compatible exploded multipart GLB assets are normalized independently per source part with exact-coordinate evidence; parts are never welded to one another and generated closure faces retain non-source provenance.

With face-count reduction disabled, a fully normalized compatible multipart part may use a resolution-independent inherited-source warning only after every retained triangle is proven to be an exact-coordinate multiset subset of the imported part; QEM, joints, coordinate movement, incomplete proof, and generated-cap intersections remain ineligible.

The inherited-source warning is not a repair: every mandatory solid check must pass, all complete self-intersection IDs must remain in an externally anchored source prefix, the affected count is bounded by max(100, ceil(source_faces / 100)), and affected area is bounded to 0.002 of the part.

Multipart 3MF export rechecks the exact binary64 millimetre coordinates written to the archive and externally anchors source-face ranges, per-part QEM limits, and self-intersection records against coordinated metadata relabeling.

Per-part 3MF export rebases each selected part to local part ID zero and projects only complete live multipart proof; local repair caps and shared-interface caps retain distinct provenance, and incomplete or stale mappings fail closed.
When export finds an eligible unsolidified model, ChromaMatter announces the safe solidification step, runs it, and resumes export only after success.
Manual paint state and adaptive trees keep exact ordered-face carry across the seam-only vertex remap.
Strict 3MF topology validation checks all type=model resources, including printable child objects that are not direct build items.
A bounded minor self-intersection introduced by QEM is a warning only after all mandatory solid checks pass, and the export guide requires Snapmaker Orca project-open and slice-preview confirmation.
Combined and per-part 3MF output retain physical F1-F4 and stable canonical palette-state semantics.

Export records a stable Full Spectrum layer-cycle and prime-tower baseline while keeping experimental Local Z, advanced dithering, and pointillism disabled and leaving support selection to Snapmaker Orca.
